extracted.intended_audience: NIH-funded researchers, grant applicants, program officers, and peer reviewers (biomedical research community)
extracted.subtask_description: Assessment and commentary on the NIH R21 exploratory/developmental grant mechanism, focusing on its intended purpose, how applications are reviewed, and policy/program fixes to make it function as intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 purpose: exploratory/developmental research
rubrics_metrics.description: The R21 grant mechanism is intended to encourage exploratory and developmental research by providing two years of support for the early and conceptual stages of research project development. The NIH has standardized the Exploratory/Developmental Grant (R21) application characteristics, requirements, preparation, and review procedures in order to accommodate investigator-initiated (unsolicited) grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R21s are meant to facilitate later R01s by supporting early-stage work and preliminary studies; applicants and reviewers should evaluate R21s against this exploratory/developmental purpose rather than as full-scale R01 projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 as a means to obtain preliminary data for R01s
rubrics_metrics.description: The R21 grant is meant to facilitate the award of larger regular research project grant (R01) applications by providing investigators with limited funds and time to pursue initial studies to obtain preliminary data for larger, more fully developed research projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success of R21s should be measured in part by whether they enable subsequent, fundable R01s; program officers might track R21-to-R01 progression as an outcome metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-preliminary-data expectation (intent vs. practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are they serious about the no-preliminary-data thing? how can they be when the 'best' grants all have supporting evidence...?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The R21 is intended to support work that may lack preliminary data; reviewer expectations that demand substantial preliminary evidence are an anti-pattern. Possible remedies include removing preliminary data expectations for R21s or explicitly instructing reviewers not to penalize lack of prelim data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review R21s in dedicated study sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Perhaps by putting them in their own sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dedicated R21-only study sections (or RFAs with their own review panels) can focus on exploratory/innovative aspects and avoid applying R01 standards; NCI and some NIAID examples show this can work, with SRO/Chair intervention when preliminary data are being over-emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit reviewer instructions to treat R21 differently
rubrics_metrics.description: Perhaps by a series of reviewer instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH should provide clear written guidance to reviewers on how R21s differ from R01s (evaluation criteria, role of preliminary data, acceptable risk), since reviewers are capable of altering behavior when given explicit instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize follow-on R01s from successful R21s
rubrics_metrics.description: Or, maybe, by prioritizing any R01 that arose from a successful R21 interval?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an incentive and measure of mechanism effectiveness, programs could give favorable consideration or some priority to R01 applications that directly build on previously funded R21 exploratory work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and feedback on R21 review outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH could fix a lot of the bad study section behavior just by shining a bright light upon it. ... telling study sections they weren't (obviously) doing the intended job of treating it like a different mechanism from the R01 and urging them to do better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular reporting to study sections and program leadership about R21 scoring patterns and outcomes can expose misalignment and drive corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid killing a mechanism without fixing root causes
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a desired goal, and the thing you thought would accomplish that goal isn't getting the job done, you might want to fix or replace it. Otherwise someone might conclude you aren't really interested in the goal in the first place. ... Throwing up their hands and closing out the mechanism is no solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy decisions (e.g., terminating a FOA) should be preceded by attempts to correct review practice, structure, and incentives; alternatives and root-cause fixes should be considered before elimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-pattern: treating R21 as a 'mini R01' in review
rubrics_metrics.description: The recent trend is that reviewer looks for a mini RO1 in R21. ... reviewed with essentially the same criteria as R01s, and not surprisingly scored terribly by comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a common reviewer bias that undermines mechanism intent; review panels should be steered away from R01-like expectations (e.g., extensive preliminary data, fully developed aims) when evaluating R21s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance study section composition: scientific specificity vs mechanism specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Perhaps the smaller ICs are pleading that there are not enough R21s in close enough topic domains to get proper review. Biasing for scientific specificity over mechanism specificity?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program managers must consider whether to organize reviews by scientific domain (topic) or by mechanism (R21) and find ways (e.g., cross-IC coordination, clustered RFAs) to ensure appropriate reviewer expertise while preserving mechanism-specific evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect and effectively support junior investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Take note of the long failed history of the R29/FIRST, NI checkbox, ESI focus, etc attempts to help out the junior investigators. It has quite obviously been an issue with the NIH since at least the 80s ... None of that kept study sections from beating up the junior faculty to an unfair degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism design and review practices should include safeguards and structural measures to ensure early-career investigators are not unfairly disadvantaged by review behaviors that favor established applicants or demand extensive preliminary data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use funding allocation to influence mechanism effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: R21s are half the price of R01s, broadly speaking. Fewer apps too. They could make their overall R-mech success rates look better by putting more $$ into the R21s and funding fewer R01s....
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjusting budgetary allocations (more R21 dollars, fewer R01s) can change portfolio outcomes and study section behavior; program-level funding strategy is a lever to achieve intended mechanism impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-side fit assessment and timing considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a great idea that is a perfect fit for an R21....maybe? Somebody has to get the last one.... (and commenters asked whether it's worth sending an A0 for the upcoming Oct deadline, now that there's no chance for an A1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should carefully judge whether their proposal truly fits the exploratory, preliminary-data-light scope of an R21 and consider timing (last receipt dates, resubmission opportunities) before submitting.
